reader.requirement: At 85 a space may optionally follow any separator except the opening quotation mark (where it is literal content); a punctuation character inside a PICTURE character-string or numeric literal is a symbol of that string (including the comma decimal point under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA), a PICTURE string ends only at a space, comma, semicolon or period separator; and separator rules do not apply inside nonnumeric literals, comment-entries or comment lines.

edition-consulted.switches: the comment-entry paragraphs (AUTHOR, DATE-WRITTEN, ...) are accepted at 85 and refused from 2002 (COBOL0902); the comment-entry text itself is discarded by the logical conversion at every edition
a floating-point numeric literal (2002) is refused at 85 (COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Version|Year|dialect in SeparatorRule.cs, PictureSeparatorPeriodRule.cs, the lexer's separator and PICMODE rules and ReferenceFormatProcessor's comment-entry set: none reads the edition; the two edition reads are VersionConformancePass construct gates for forms outside or beyond 1985's rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: comment-entries exist at 85 (their content is exempt from separator rules) and are refused from 2002; floating-point literals are refused at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f03_01 and 1985-SR-IV_4_2_1-9 cover a space after the opening quote, '.' and ',' in a PICTURE, a PICTURE ended by a semicolon, separators inside a literal and a comment line; not exercised: comment-entries, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA literals and pictures, a signed decimal literal, the refusal of a PICTURE not delimited by a separator, a space after '(' ',' ':'

probes.printed: $1.234,50 / 00,25 / E3 OK / ( "==; ,.) / [Q  ] / 03,00 (the program's own .out expected ' $1.234,50'; the printed '$1.234,50' is right, since the first $ of $$.$$9,99 is the currency position and 1234 fills the four digit positions)
probes.expected: AUTHOR and DATE-WRITTEN comment-entries holding an unbalanced quote, ==, parentheses, ; and , compile; under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA the literals 1234,5 / +,25 / -1,5 / 2,0 / -2,9 and pictures $$.$$9,99 / 99,99 / S9(3)V99 read the comma as decimal point; PIC ...; VALUE and PIC X(3), VALUE end the PICTURE at the separator; separators inside a literal are content; ( 1 + 2 ) with spaces after '('

probes.expected: a comma with no space after it is no separator, so PIC X(3),VALUE is one PICTURE character-string; refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR9  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR9

reader.notes: PIC_STRING takes every non-space character and backs off a trailing period, comma or semicolon only when a space follows it, which is exactly SR9's delimiting rule; comment-entry text never reaches the lexer at 85. The one probe difference (sr9-002) was the probe author's expected value for a floating insertion picture, not the compiler.
